title: Yara and the Monsoon
premise: Jonah Iversen, a disgraced mountain guide, takes one last contract escorting a cartographer named Yara through a coastal range where the receding tide has exposed a cave tied to an old smuggling legend. Inside they find evidence that the mining concession propping up the local town was built on forged permits — and the company's enforcers want them silenced before the season's first snow seals the passes. Pursued across the high country with winter closing in, Jonah must choose between fleeing alone and standing as witness for a community that reminds him why he once loved guiding. They cross the range ahead of the snows and deliver the proof to a regional tribunal, clearing Yara's father's name and giving Jonah a reason to stop running.
about_author: E. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former trail crew leader who spent a decade mapping remote coastlines before turning to fiction. Their stories explore people who live just outside the reach of official systems.

chapters.title: The Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Broke and blacklisted, Jonah accepts Yara's contract to survey a coastal cave revealed by an unprecedented low tide. Inside, they discover ledgers proving the Vale Mining concession rests on forged permits — and signs someone else searched here recently. The emotional beat is wary hope: two outsiders recognizing in each other the same habit of not belonging anywhere.

chapters.title: Permits Expire at Dusk
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The company's enforcers burn their camp and seize their maps, forcing them into the high passes weeks early. Yara reveals she isn't just a cartographer — her father died disputing these very permits, and she needs the ledgers to clear his name. The beat is rising dread mixed with resolve: the escape route becomes a mission neither can abandon.

chapters.title: Ahead of the Snows
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A storm chases them onto a glacier crossing where a rope bridge fails; Jonah nearly falls saving the ledgers, and Yara hauls him back, reversing their roles of protector and protected. Cornered at a ranger station, they broadcast copies of the documents to a regional tribunal before the enforcers arrive. The climax trades on trust finally earned at altitude.

chapters.title: What the Mountain Keeps
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Snowbound but alive, they descend to find the town rallying around the leaked evidence; the tribunal suspends the concession and posthumously exonerates Yara's father. Offered a chance to vanish again, Jonah instead stays to testify — his first act of standing still in years. The resolution lands on belonging: home is a choice made, not a place found.
